[RFCS.6.6] Across every atom that carries it — `FactAssert` ([RFCS.6.2])
and `ClockAdvance` ([RFCS.10.2]) — `clock_ns` is the
engine **monotonic** clock (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`-class; relative, not a
calendar time). Replay re-drives the engine clock from the recorded
`clock_ns` values. A stream's **start** is the first atom's `clock_ns`,
its **end** is the last atom's `clock_ns`, and its execution
**duration** is `end − start`; because the end is whichever atom was
written last, a truncated stream still reports its duration up to the
point it stopped. The nanosecond unit is not an accuracy guarantee —
effective resolution is platform-bounded and low digits may be zero —
so a reader must order events by `seq` ([LFST.5.3]), never by
`clock_ns` low-bits. An encoder writes `clock_ns` on every atom that carries
it ([RFCS.3.3]): replay re-drives the clock from it.
